A warm welcome to Nepal. The shorter expression “Swagat chha” means “Welcome.”
A simple expression of thanks, for a shared moment or a kindness along the way.
Tea. A lovely word to know in the tea hills or over a shared cup; it does not describe one particular recipe.
Slowly. Let it be a small reminder to make time for the people and places along your journey.

cautions: Nepali and Sanskrit are different languages. A Sanskrit-rooted word may also be ordinary Nepali vocabulary; label the context rather than claiming exclusive ownership.
Nepal is multilingual. Do not call these nine words all of Nepal’s language or imply all communities have identical customs.
Keep English meanings visible and mark actual phrases with lang=ne or lang=sa. Use a Devanagari-capable font; do not apply wide Latin letter-spacing to Devanagari.
Use common words as elegant editorial touches, not as unintelligible replacements for practical navigation, controls or form labels.
Roman spellings are readable transliterations rather than exact pronunciation instructions; no audio was generated or verified.
Do not invent historical provenance for an original slogan. Label any Sanskrit line with its actual source and distinguish a paraphrase from a literal translation.
Prefer the short hospitality line over scattering Om signs or sacred mantras as decoration.
